items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: We only had four saxophones -- Lester, Jack Washington, Earl.

ctx.x: Was there a model that you had like for trying to get the kind of sound that you wanted?

Yeah, I wanted to get an even vibrato, but I wanted it to be pretty, you know, like there were some good saxophone players in those days that played beautiful and like Frank O'Bannon had a beautiful sound. He was a beautiful -- he would have made a beautiful first player. And like Earl has got a beautiful sound, Earl Warren, for first, you understand what I mean? And he can play those pretty things, you know. I wanted to sound like that. I was always conscious of trying to get a sound because everybody like was…

So after the band started, we started playing -- the band became so popular and we started playing other towns, like in Oklahoma and all around, you know. We'd go as far as Oklahoma City and we went to Kansas City a couple of times. We thought that was really it then, you know, we thought we really had it made.
